sentences.text: Revenue rose from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025, a 4.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F205].
Growth came in steps, not steady compounding: revenue rose 19.8% in FY2020 [D183] and 13.3% in FY2021 [D230], then fell in each of the last three years [D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 jump reflected a 19.3% comparable sales increase and new stores [P51][D183].
Operating margin fell 4.9pp in FY2022 to 3.5% [D290][F31], which the filing ties to markdowns, cancelled orders and inventory costs [P38].
Merchandise sales fell 2.0% in FY2025 [D466], subtracting 2.0pp from total revenue growth [D467].
Food & beverage grew 1.3% in FY2025 [D507] and is now 23.0% of revenue [D506], while Apparel & accessories subtracted 0.7pp [D565].
Comparable sales fell 2.6%, driven by a 2.2% traffic decline [P14], matching the 1.7% revenue fall in FY2025 [D416].
Revenue growth ran 0.4pp below operating-cost growth [D439], so operating income fell 8.1% on a 1.7% sales decline [D417][D416].
Over the window, diluted EPS compounded at 6.3% against 3.4% for net income [F210][F208], as diluted shares fell from 582.5 million [X107] to 455.6 million [X116].
Operating margin of 4.9% is below its 5.6% window median and just above the 4.7% retail peer median [F34][D590][D607].
Operating margin fell 0.3pp in FY2025 [D429], as cost of revenue took 0.3pp [D440] and SG&A added 0.1pp [D441].
The SG&A benefit reflected a 0.6-point interchange settlement gain, partly offset by deleverage on lower sales [P11][D441].
Cost of revenue explained a 4.6pp drop in FY2022 [D301] and reversed by 3.0pp in FY2023 [D347].
Net margin of 3.5% sits 1.4pp below operating margin [F54][F34]; net interest rose to $445 million [X66] on higher average debt [P10].
Operating cash flow was 1.77x net income [D404], but free cash flow of $2.84 billion [F104] was 0.77x [D405], below the 1.01x window median [D599].
Operating cash fell 10.9% [D421], which the filing ties to lower net earnings and weaker payables leverage [P7].
Capital expenditure rose 28.9% to $3.73 billion [D423][F94], mainly for new stores and remodels [P5], at 1.19x D&A [D406].
Free cash flow margin of 2.7% [D401] trails the 4.5% window median [D596].
Net cash was -$4.30 billion [D410], or -4.1% of revenue [D411], against a peer median of -3.5% [D613], the 50th percentile of six peers [D612].
That compares with -$10.6 billion in FY2022 [D271], as cash and investments reached $10.1 billion [D408].
Buybacks and dividends absorbed 86.8% of free cash flow [D413], with repurchases down to $408 million [X126] and dividends of $2.05 billion [X136].
Return on average equity of 24.0% [D415] sits below the 28.6% retail peer median [D617].
Revenue fell three years running, by 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% [R1][D324][D370][D416], a 3-year CAGR of -1.3% [D603].
The filings tie the slide to discretionary categories weakening from 2022 [P30] and a 2.2% traffic decline in FY2025 [P14].
Free cash flow fell 36.7% in FY2025 [D422], reversing a 17.3% gain in FY2024 [D376]; lower earnings and payables leverage explain the operating side [P7].
Operating margin has slipped two years running, down 0.4pp from 5.3% in FY2023 to 4.9% in FY2025 [R4][F32][F34], a low-severity flag.
I dropped the cash-burn cover flag [R3] since FY2025 free cash flow was positive [F104], and the current-ratio flag [R2] since it sits at its window median [F184][D602].
Revenue growth staying below the FY2025 rate of -1.7% [D416] would confirm the decline; a better rate would reverse it in the FY2026 10-K.
Operating margin rising back toward the 5.6% window median [D590] from 4.9% [F34] would signal recovery in the FY2026 10-K.
Free cash flow above FY2025's $2.84 billion [F104], with 2026 capex near the guided $5 billion [P4], would confirm cash resilience in the FY2026 10-K.
